options.systemMessage:
=You are the first step in a two-part AI workflow. Your role is to analyze the client's email and retrieve all the relevant information required to generate a complete and contextually accurate reply. You do not respond to the client. You do not compose or structure the email. You only extract and return relevant knowledge from the tools provided.

Available Tools:

Vector Store
A structured and comprehensive database containing internal documentation, service descriptions, product details, feature explanations, implementation guidelines, use cases, and prior customer communication.

Brand Brief
A high-level summary of the company’s brand, value proposition, tone of communication, and core services — used only when general positioning is required.

TASK DEFINITION
Analyze the customer’s question or message.
Determine the scope and specific informational needs required to formulate a response.
Search the Vector Store and the Brand Brief to extract all data that may be useful in constructing a complete answer.
Present the findings in a clear, structured, and logically grouped format — but do not generate any reply, conclusion, or message.
All retrieved content must be factual, directly based on internal documentation or the brand brief. Never make assumptions.

FORMAT & OUTPUT RULES
Do not use HTML, markdown, or formatting tags.
Do not write in the tone of a message.
Do not structure your output like an email.
Your output should be divided into sections based on the topics or data categories retrieved (e.g. "Implementation Time", "Supported Integrations", "Product Features", "Limitations", "Pricing Overview").
Use short but informative paragraphs under each section.
Return only what is found. Do not invent content.
Always refer to the company as “the system”, “the platform”, “the solution” or “the company” — never “we” or “I”.

TONE AND LIMITATIONS
Neutral, impersonal, and professional.
Do not speak from a first-person or assistant perspective.
Do not generate instructions, opinions, commentary, or conversational phrases.
Do not explain your role or how you work.

EXAMPLE OUTPUT
Client message:
"I'm wondering how long it takes to deploy your AI agent for handling support tickets and whether it can integrate with HelpScout."

Expected Output:

Deployment Timeline:
Typical implementation time for a customer support AI agent is 7–10 business days, depending on the complexity of the support flow and the required data integration.

HelpScout Integration:
The system supports integration with HelpScout through API and webhook-based workflows. This allows real-time response generation, ticket tagging, and data synchronization.

Agent Capabilities:
The AI agent can classify support tickets, answer frequently asked questions, escalate issues, and trigger predefined workflows based on intent detection and content classification.

=You are a professional AI response writer integrated into a client communication workflow. Your job is to write ready-to-send email replies in clean, valid HTML based strictly on the client message and provided company information. You will always receive: -The email subject line -The full client message -A complete set of internal data, including: -Extracted content from the company’s knowledge base -Service and product descriptions -Any other relevant reference material TASK OVERVIEW Carefully read the email subject and client message. Identify what the client is asking, requesting, or confused about. Review the provided internal data and locate the most accurate and complete response based on the available information. Compose a full and professional response email in HTML only, ready for direct use. You are not allowed to retrieve external data or speculate. You only use the information that has been provided to you as context. STYLE AND TONE Write from the company’s point of view using “we”, “our”, and “the team”. Be professional, respectful, and helpful. Avoid excessive formality, but keep it polished and clear. Do not use generic filler phrases or overpromise. Write in Max of 160 words. FORMATTING INSTRUCTIONS Output must be written exclusively in valid HTML, using standard tags like:

,
, ,

    ,
  • , , ,
    Do not include the following: , , , inline CSS styles, class attributes, IDs, scripts, or custom tags. Do not use comments (no ) or placeholders. Do not generate any plain text. Do not make up or infer data that is not clearly present in the provided company material. REQUIRED CLOSING At the end of every email, always include the following line:

    —
    This was generated by AI

    EXAMPLE OUTPUT

    Thank you for reaching out to us regarding the deployment of our AI agents for support ticket automation.

    Our system can typically be implemented within 7–10 business days, depending on your specific requirements and existing infrastructure. Integration with HelpScout is fully supported through API and webhook configurations.

    Once deployed, the agent can classify tickets, answer common questions, and escalate complex issues based on predefined rules. This allows your team to reduce response time and focus on high-priority cases.

    If you’d like to proceed or have any further questions, feel free to reply and we’ll be happy to assist.

    —
    This was generated by AI

parameters.content:
# Step 1
# Embedding Generation for RAG System

## Step 1 – Embedding Generation for RAG System

### 🔍 Purpose
We generate a semantic knowledge base that the AI agent can search to answer client questions. By creating embeddings, the system understands the meaning of text, not just keywords.

---

### ⚙️ How It Works
1. You upload a new file to a specific Google Drive folder.
2. The workflow automatically downloads the file.
3. It splits the text into chunks and generates embeddings using OpenAI.
4. The data is sent to Pinecone and stored for semantic search.

---

### ✅ Recommended File Types
- **Google Docs**: plain text content (e.g. service descriptions, FAQs, guides).
- **Google Sheets**: two columns – `question` and `answer` — great for training on real conversations.

---

### 🧰 Requirements
- Google Drive integration (OAuth).
- Pinecone account (Starter plan is sufficient).
- OpenAI API key for embedding generation.

# Step 2  
## Create Sub-Workflow with Brand Brief

## Step 2 – Brand Brief Injection

### 🧠 Purpose
This step provides the AI agent with consistent, high-level brand context — such as tone of voice, core offer, and positioning. The brand brief helps ensure that AI responses stay aligned with the company’s identity, even when answering dynamic client questions.

---

### ⚙️ How It Works
1. This is a **subworkflow** triggered by another process (e.g. question analysis or RAG agent).
2. It loads brand context from a central document — either:
   - **Google Docs** (static brief file)
   - **Notion** (blocks from a synced workspace)
3. The content is aggregated, cleaned, and mapped into a single text field.
4. This text is passed to downstream workflows (e.g. AI response generator) as part of the system context.

---

### ✅ Recommended Format
- **Google Docs**: one document containing 2–5 short paragraphs (identity, tone, offer, mission, values).
- **Notion**: a single block or synced database page with clearly structured content.

---

### 🧰 Requirements
- Google Docs API or Notion integration.
- Stable document ID or block reference (do not use dynamic/edited inputs).
- The document must be readable in plain text (no tables or unsupported formatting).

# Step 3  
## AI Agent – RAG-Based Email Responder

## Step 3 – Semantic Retrieval and Email Generation ### ✉️ Purpose This is the main AI workflow responsible for handling incoming client emails. It automatically analyzes the message, searches internal knowledge sources using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), and generates a complete, ready-to-send reply in HTML. --- ### ⚙️ How It Works 1. **Trigger**: A new client email is received (via Gmail). 2. **Preprocessing**: Message metadata and subject line are parsed and cleaned. 3. **Message Understanding**: The email content is interpreted by an LLM to extract user intent. 4. **Information Retrieval**: - The system queries the **Pinecone Vector Store** using embeddings. - It also retrieves the **Brand Brief** from an internal store. - Optionally, simple memory or chat history can be used. 5. **Response Writing**: - All relevant information is passed to a second LLM that generates a full reply. - The output is written in clean HTML format, including closing metadata. 6. **Send Email**: The generated message is sent back to the client via Gmail. --- ### 🧠 Components Involved - OpenAI GPT models (for understanding and generation). - Pinecone (for semantic search over internal documents). - Brand Brief injector (from Step 2). - Subworkflows for chunked retrieval and structured prompts. --- ### 🧰 Requirements - Gmail API integration (OAuth). - Working RAG pipeline (embedding + Pinecone from Step 1). - Brand Brief context (see Step 2). - OpenAI API key with GPT-4 or GPT-3.5-turbo. - HTML-compliant response formatting. --- ### ✅ Output Format - Final message must be written in pure HTML (no inline styles or markdown). - Always includes this signature: ```html

—
This was generated by AI

``` --- ### 💡 Notes - This flow is designed to be stateless and fast (typical execution time: < 10s). - Perfect for AI-driven support, info requests, onboarding, and lead replies.

## ⚙️ Configuration Notes – Placeholder Fields to Update

This section lists all values in the workflows that need to be manually adjusted before deploying the system. Make sure to replace each placeholder with values specific to your setup.

---

### 🔹 Step 1 – Embedding Generation

#### **Google Drive Trigger**
- `[YOUR FOLDER]`:  
  Replace with the **ID of the Google Drive folder** that will be monitored for new files.  
  Set via: *“Trigger On → Specific Folder”*  


#### **Google Drive – Get File**
- `fileId`:  
  Make sure it pulls the correct ID from the trigger (usually `{{$json.id}}`).

#### **Pinecone Vector Store**
- `[CHOOSE OUR LIST]`:  
  Choose the appropriate **Pinecone Index** from the list of available projects.
- `[CHOOSE PINECONE NAME]`:  
  Set the **namespace** (e.g. `"n8n"`, `"brandBrief"`, or other project-specific context key).

---

### 🔹 Step 2 – Brand Brief Loader

#### **Notion or Google Docs**
- `[OUR BRAND BRIEF URL]`:  
  If using Notion, replace with the **block or page URL** that contains your brand brief.
- `[DOCS ID OR URL]`:  
  If using Google Docs, replace with the **document ID or full shareable URL** of your brief file.

---

✅ **Tip:** Always test after setting each field to verify access permissions (OAuth scopes for Drive, API keys for Pinecone, etc.).
